chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-'Ala' al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Any man who wishes to free his female slave and marry her, and make her manumission her dowry, may do so.

key_terms.عِتْق: Manumission or freeing of a slave
key_terms.فَعَلَ: He did so / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a master's manumission of his female slave serve as her dowry in marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the permissibility of a master freeing his female slave (umm al-walid or otherwise) and marrying her, with the manumission itself serving as her dowry (mahr). It highlights a specific legal mechanism in Shia jurisprudence that simplifies the transaction by merging the act of liberation with the marital contract, reflecting the flexibility in early Islamic family law. The narration, transmitted through the chain of al-Tusi, underscores the practical application of these rulings in consolidating social and economic ties within the household.
